Inadmissibility of Judicial Division for Unauthorized Buildings An heir initiated a lawsuit to dissolve the inheritance community regarding a three-story building, with the consent of the other co-heirs. However, a technical expert (C.T.U.) determined that the second floor of the property was built without a valid building permit, rendering it partially "abusivo". The legal classification involves the dissolution of inheritance (Art. 713 c.c.) in relation to urban planning compliance. The interpretative challenge is whether a court can order the division of an asset that violates building regulations. The Court ruled that the judicial division of a property is prohibited if the asset is structurally illegal, as the court cannot facilitate the transfer of assets lacking administrative regularity, leading to the rejection of the claim.
 Revocation of Legal Aid for Gross Negligence During the proceedings, it emerged that the plaintiff and one defendant had been granted state-funded legal aid. The legal issue concerns the criteria for revoking such benefits under Art. 136 of the T.U. Spese di Giustizia. The interpretative problem is whether initiating or joining a division lawsuit for an illegal property constitutes "gross negligence." The Court determined that acting without verifying the basic urban planning status of the inheritance mass represents a conduct of "colpa grave" (gross negligence). Consequently, the Court ordered the revocation of the state-funded legal aid for the parties involved, as they had burdened the judicial system with an inadmissible claim.
